entries.title: dev-compare: window and field contracts (Python)
entries.summary: Small dependency-free Python repo defining two contracts: half-open windows [start, end) and an order-preserving Fields index map with a separate visible-names view, plus a resolver that adds a parent offset. Tests run with python3 -B test_contract.py.
entries.body:
Layout (flat, root only): README.md, window.py, fields.py, resolver.py, test_contract.py.

Window contract: window.contains(start, end, value) returns start <= value < end. The start is inclusive and the end is exclusive. Adjacent windows must not both accept their shared boundary. The test asserts contains(10,20,10) and contains(10,20,19) are true and contains(10,20,20) is false (message "END_EXCLUSIVE").

Field contract: Fields(fields) takes an iterable of (name, hidden) pairs and stores them as a tuple in original order, including hidden fields. It builds one immutable MappingProxyType name->index map over all fields, so index_of(name) is stable across repeated calls and raises KeyError for unknown names. visible_names() is a separate filtered tuple of non-hidden names. It is a view only and must never be used as an index namespace.

Resolver: resolver.resolve(fields, name, parent_offset) returns (relation_index, hierarchy_index). relation_index is the all-fields index. hierarchy_index is that index plus parent_offset. The current code calls index_of twice rather than reusing relation_index.

Testing: dependency-free unittest in test_contract.py, run with `python3 -B test_contract.py`. Tests cover the window boundaries and a two-field case (hidden then visible) where visible_names() == ("value",), index_of("value") == 1 (hidden fields still count), and resolve(fields, "value", 3) == (1, 4).

When changing code here, preserve the half-open window semantics and keep hidden fields counted in indexes.

claims.text: Windows include their start and exclude their end ([start, end)); adjacent windows must not both accept the shared boundary.
window.contains is implemented as start <= value < end and the test asserts the end value is rejected.
Fields keeps original order including hidden fields; index_of reads one immutable map (MappingProxyType) and returns the same index on repeated calls.
visible_names is a separate filtered view and is never an index namespace; hidden fields still consume indexes.
resolve returns (all-fields index, all-fields index + parent_offset); it calls index_of twice instead of reusing the first result.
Tests are dependency-free unittest, run with `python3 -B test_contract.py`; there is no CI config, packaging or contributing guide in the frozen tree.

Limitation: test coverage is minimal (one window case, one field case). Duplicate field names, unknown names and non-integer offsets are untested, and behavior for duplicate names (later index wins in the dict comprehension) is inferred from code, not documented.

1  from types import MappingProxyType
2  
3  
4  class Fields:
5      def __init__(self, fields):
6          self._fields = tuple(fields)
7          self._indexes = MappingProxyType({name: index for index, (name, hidden) in enumerate(self._fields)})
8  
9      def index_of(self, name):
10          return self._indexes[name]
11  
12      def visible_names(self):
13          return tuple(name for name, hidden in self._fields if not hidden)
